paragraphs: Minga sells one platform that K-12 schools use to run the daily operations of a campus. The sales argument is that it replaces six separate vendors with a single connected system. The company says over 2,500 schools and 750 districts across the USA use it.

Tardy handling replaces the morning line with an ID scan that marks a student late and sends them to their seat. Follow-up is automated, with alerts and consequences that also keep families informed. On the behavior side, staff recognize positive behavior in three clicks and award PBIS points instantly. Parents can see a child's daily wins through instant notifications. Student, staff, bell schedule and class data sync from existing systems through MingaSync. The company says a school can be live in as little as two weeks.

Case studies name Allen High in Texas, which the site calls the largest high school in the state. Another describes Paul Laurence Dunbar High School tackling chronic absenteeism and student accountability. A testimonial on the tardy page claims a nine week year over year comparison showed tardies down 87 percent.
